root_idea.summary: The root has several classical branches: uncovering or exposing, flight or turning away, a class of young animals, and lightness or agitation. The Quranic forms chiefly represent the flight-and-escape branch.
root_idea.development: The lexical tradition relates flight to the broader notion of uncovering or moving away, while also recognizing separate animal and lightness/agitation branches rather than deriving every meaning from one direct Quranic sense.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the verbal-noun citation form فِرَار.
Displayed under the normalized place/action noun مَفَرّ.

senses.definition: To flee or turn away in order to escape.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of fleeing from something feared or threatening; with إِلَى, it can express fleeing or turning toward a refuge or destination, including فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ.

senses.definition: Fleeing; flight; the act or state of turning away to escape.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of فَرَّ, used for flight or fleeing in general and in constructions describing escape from danger or rejection of a summons.
In أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ, the form can be understood as asking where or what the escape is, including the act of fleeing.

senses.definition: A place or time of fleeing; a place or occasion to which one flees.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ also permits place and time interpretations; the cited modern location is supplied by QAC.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wheel widely away from an enemy in order to turn back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional fleeing-and-returning construction, distinct from simple flight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or betake oneself to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional construction expressing movement toward a destination; it is broader than the Quranic refuge-oriented use represented under the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the arm or hand to fall off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic bodily-use expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To examine an animal's teeth by exposing them, especially to determine its age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of examining a horse or other beast's teeth, and of opening a horse's mouth for that purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To examine, scrutinize, investigate, or inquire into an affair or a person's inner thoughts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of examining; may take an affair or a person as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an affair to return to its beginning and recommence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic, figurative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intelligent after having been weak in mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare classical intransitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To investigate another's state while that person investigates one's own.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal or mutually directed investigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or something flee or turn away in order to escape.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative use; the object may be a person or another animate being.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause an arm or hand to fall off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic bodily-use expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To split or cleave someone's head with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels or horses to shed their milk teeth and grow replacements.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of animals undergoing the indicated stage of dentition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To laugh at, deride, or ridicule someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V idiomatic use with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flee from one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smile broadly or beautifully so as to show the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII expression for smiling without loud or prolonged laughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For lightning to glisten or flash.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of showing the teeth in a smile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To snuff or draw a thing up into the nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate transitive Form VIII use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put something into motion, agitation, or commotion; to shake it about.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reduplicated Form I use, including the motion of a bit in a horse's mouth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break, cut, split, slit, rend, tear, or mangle something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The listed uses range from breaking or cutting to violently mangling an object or animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To defame someone or mangle his reputation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of tearing or mangling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disparage or discommend something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, including disparaging the enjoyments of the present world.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call, cry, or call out to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive or directed vocal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a camel to agitate or shake its body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive animal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a horse to strike its teeth against the bit and move its head about.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive equine use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or go with short steps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive movement use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be light-minded, unsteady, or foolishly hasty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of mental or behavioral lightness and haste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak confusedly or profusely; loquacity or excessive talk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb describes confused or abundant speech, while فَرْفَرَةٌ can denote talk itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the vehicle or women's saddle called فَرْفَار.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized denominative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle a fire with the wood of the tree called فَرْفَار.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use associated with the named tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The best or choice member of a people, group, or stock of property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a chief or select person and, by extension, the choicest animals or possessions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beginning or first part of heat, or its vehemence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may denote either the onset or intensity of heat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confusion and difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for falling into confusion or difficulty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner of smiling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in describing the quality or beauty of someone's smile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young sheep, goat, cow, or wild bovine; especially a small-bodied young animal or a weaned lamb or kid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can function as a singular or plural designation in the reported classical usages; the exact animal varies by authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who habitually avoids whatever might induce suspicion or an evil opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional epithet applied to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or base of the mane on a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical equine term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mouth, especially that of a horse or similar animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use reported for an equine context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A defeated military force or troop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression كَتِيبَةٌ فُرَّى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman beautiful in the front teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine epithet concerning the appearance of the front teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quicksilver or mercury.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized name motivated by its flowing rapidly and not remaining in one place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spinning top, a child's toy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A diminutive form used for the toy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fugitive or one who is fleeing; by intensification, one who flees much or very readily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet for one or more persons, including females; the form can function as an epithet or quasi-plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A breaker or mangler of everything; specifically, a lion that mangles its antagonist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lion designation is a conventional epithet based on the animal's manner of attacking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light and unsteady in mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use, with a feminine form in ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loquacious, talkative, or a great talker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use comparable to ثَرْثَارٌ, with a feminine form in ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard, durable species of tree whose wood is used for vessels and other objects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical and material-culture term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vehicle or saddle for women or pastors, resembling a howdah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fat, weaned young lamb or kid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted evidence includes a noted camel/lamb textual discrepancy; the young-livestock sense is presented cautiously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A youth or young man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension likening a youth to a well-fed young animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small bird, especially a sparrow or similar passerine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also reported for certain other small birds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Parched meal prepared from the fruit of the yanbūt tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized food term, also reported under closely related pronunciations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Purple or violet, and the violet flower or color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the color or the flower associated with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Purslane.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate plant designation reported in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Purple-colored.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisba adjective, including use for a purple flower.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that moves or agitates the bit in its mouth in order to disengage it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An equine epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough, ungentle, or uncouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Days that reveal or cause news and tidings to spread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse fit for fleeing or excellent in fleeing, ready to return to the fight and flee again.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrumental noun used as an equine epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Examined, investigated, searched into, or interrogated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial form associated with the investigative use of فَرَّ.

cautions: مَفَرّ in 75:10 has an explicitly reported ambiguity between the act of fleeing and a place or time of fleeing; the example therefore links both numbered senses.
The young-animal evidence under فُرْفُورٌ contains a noted transmitted camel/lamb discrepancy and is stated cautiously rather than normalized beyond the evidence.
